characters.name: Ulysses
characters.description: Ithacan king and the poem's protagonist; veteran of the Trojan War, long-absent husband of Penelope and father of Telemachus

characters.name: Penelope
characters.description: Wife of Ulysses, queen of Ithaca; central figure enduring suitors and awaiting her husband's return

characters.name: Telemachus
characters.description: Son of Ulysses and Penelope, who undertakes a journey to seek news of his father and later helps him reclaim the house

characters.name: Laertes
characters.description: Father of Ulysses, elderly inhabitant of the Ithacan farm who is reunited with his son

characters.name: Minerva
characters.description: Goddess (Athena) who aids and disguises Ulysses and Telemachus; takes multiple forms in the narrative

characters.name: Jove
characters.description: King of the gods (Zeus), presides over divine council and acts as arbiter in the narrative

characters.name: Neptune
characters.description: Sea-god (Poseidon) who persecutes Ulysses because his son Polyphemus was blinded

characters.name: Mercury
characters.description: Messenger god (Hermes) who conveys divine orders and appears to mortals

characters.name: Calypso
characters.description: Nymph who keeps Ulysses on her island (Ogygia) and offers him immortality

characters.name: Circe
characters.description: Powerful Aeaean enchantress who turns some of Ulysses' men into pigs and later hosts and advises him

characters.name: Teiresias
characters.description: Blind Theban prophet consulted in Hades who gives Ulysses prophecies about his return

characters.name: Nestor
characters.description: King of Pylos, an elder Achaean who receives Telemachus and recounts aspects of the return of the Greeks

characters.name: Menelaus
characters.description: King of Sparta (Lacedaemon), host to Telemachus who relates his own wanderings and what he learned of Ulysses

characters.name: Helen
characters.description: Helen of Troy; Menelaus' wife, whose actions and gifts play a role in Telemachus' reception

characters.name: Alcinous
characters.description: King of the Phaeacians who hospitably receives Ulysses and ultimately provides him a ship and escort home

characters.name: Arete
characters.description: Queen of the Phaeacians, wife of Alcinous, influential in deciding how Ulysses is treated

characters.name: Nausicaa
characters.description: Daughter of Alcinous, Phaeacian princess who finds Ulysses washed ashore and aids him

characters.name: Demodocus
characters.description: The bard of the Phaeacians whose songs move Ulysses to tears

characters.name: Argos
characters.description: Ulysses’ old dog, who recognizes him on his return and then dies

characters.name: Euryclea
characters.description: Loyal old nurse of Ulysses and Telemachus who recognizes Ulysses by his scar while washing his feet

characters.name: Eumaeus
characters.description: The swineherd of Ulysses; faithful servant who shelters the disguised hero and helps reclaim the house

characters.name: Philoetius
characters.description: Cowherd/stockman loyal to Ulysses who assists in retaking the house

characters.name: Melanthius
characters.description: Goatherd who betrays Ulysses and supplies the suitors with arms; severely punished

characters.name: Antinous
characters.description: Leading and most aggressive of Penelope's suitors; first killed by Ulysses

characters.name: Eurymachus
characters.description: One of the principal suitors; attempts to negotiate after Antinous' death

characters.name: Amphinomus
characters.description: A suitor of Penelope noted for being comparatively decent; nevertheless killed among the suitors

characters.name: Antiphus
characters.description: Named son of Aegyptius who was killed by the Cyclops Polyphemus (recounted in Ulysses’ tale)

characters.name: Aegisthus
characters.description: Man who murdered Agamemnon (in the tale recounted by Nestor and Menelaus); foil in parallel story

characters.name: Agamemnon
characters.description: King of the Achaeans whose murder and its consequences are discussed and whose ghost appears in Hades

characters.name: Ajax
characters.description: Achaean warrior mentioned among the fallen and appearing in the underworld; prominent hero

characters.name: Achilles
characters.description: Great Achaean hero, appears in Hades and speaks with Ulysses' ghostly compatriots

characters.name: Argive Herald Medon
characters.description: Household herald who overhears the suitors' plots and is spared by Telemachus

characters.name: Phemius
characters.description: Household bard forced to sing for the suitors; spared during the slaughter

characters.name: Leiodes
characters.description: Sacrificial priest among the suitors who protests and is killed by Ulysses

characters.name: Ctesippus
characters.description: A wealthy, boorish suitor from Same who throws an ox's foot at the disguised Ulysses and is later killed

characters.name: Echephron
characters.description: One of Nestor's sons (appears helping with sacrifice at Pylos)

characters.name: Pisistratus
characters.description: Young son of Nestor who accompanies Telemachus from Pylos to Sparta and back

characters.name: Polycaste
characters.description: Youngest daughter of Nestor who washes Telemachus at Pylos

characters.name: Polyphemus
characters.description: One-eyed Cyclops who eats some of Ulysses' men; blinded by Ulysses

characters.name: Ino (Leucothea)
characters.description: Sea-nymph (formerly mortal Ino) who aids Ulysses with a veil when he is shipwrecked

characters.name: Proteus
characters.description: Old man of the sea in Egypt who tells Menelaus of other heroes' fates

characters.name: Idothea
characters.description: Daughter of Proteus who aids Menelaus (appears in Menelaus' account)

characters.name: Polydamna
characters.description: Egyptian woman who gave Helen an herb that banishes sorrow (mentioned)

characters.name: Aeolus
characters.description: Ruler of winds who gives Ulysses a bag containing adverse winds

characters.name: Laestrygonians / Antiphates
characters.description: Giant cannibal people encountered by Ulysses; Antiphates is one named Laestrygonian chief

characters.name: Elpenor
characters.description: Companion of Ulysses who dies accidentally at Circe's house and whose shade Ulysses meets in Hades

characters.name: Theoclymenus
characters.description: Seer from Argos who joins Telemachus and foretells doom to the suitors

characters.name: Autolycus
characters.description: Maternal grandfather of Ulysses; famed trickster, connected with Ulysses' childhood and the scar token

characters.name: Iphthime
characters.description: Sister of Penelope who appears as a comforting vision sent by Minerva

characters.name: Polyphemes/Polydamas/Phaedimus (named gifts)
characters.description: Various minor named figures appearing as gift-givers or referenced persons in hosts' accounts (e.g. Phaedimus, giver of a mixing bowl)

characters.name: Rhadamanthus
characters.description: Figure noted as reigning in the Elysian plain; mentioned in Menelaus' account

characters.name: Eurylochus
characters.description: Companion of Ulysses who often opposes him and leads the men who taste Circe's food; also leads men to Circe

characters.name: Dolius
characters.description: Old servant/gardener associated with Penelope's household; father of Melanthius and other sons

characters.name: Antiphates (Laestrygon)
characters.description: Named Laestrygonian king who kills some of Ulysses' men (distinct from Antiphus noted earlier)

characters.name: Philoctetes
characters.description: Archer mentioned as having excelled Ulysses in shooting during the Trojan war (referenced)

characters.name: Polyphemus' kin (Thoosa/Phorcys)
characters.description: Relatives mentioned in genealogical context (Thoosa mother of Polyphemus; Phorcys ancestor), appearing in narrative references

characters.name: Melantho
characters.description: Maid in Penelope's household who behaves insolently toward the beggar (Ulysses in disguise) and is later punished

characters.name: Nausicaa
characters.description: Phaeacian princess who encounters and aids Ulysses

characters.name: Nausithous
characters.description: Mythical figure mentioned in kinship with Polyphemus and Alcinous

characters.name: Alcinous
characters.description: King of the Phaeacians who hosts Ulysses

characters.name: Echeneus
characters.description: Phaeacian elder mentioned in council and ritual contexts

characters.name: Ulysses
characters.description: Protagonist of the narrative (Greek hero, also called Odysseus)

characters.name: Telemachus
characters.description: Son of Ulysses, central to several episodes in the story

characters.name: Penelope
characters.description: Wife of Ulysses, central figure in the homeward plotline

characters.name: Polyphemus
characters.description: A Cyclops who is son of the sea god and appears in Ulysses' wanderings

characters.name: Neptune
characters.description: Sea god (father of Polyphemus) who acts as divine antagonist

characters.name: Jove
characters.description: Sky god (Roman name for Zeus) invoked in the narrative

characters.name: Mercury
characters.description: Divine messenger (Roman name for Hermes) appearing in the text

characters.name: Minerva
characters.description: Goddess who aids Ulysses (Roman name for Athena)

characters.name: Cyclopes
characters.description: Mythical one-eyed people encountered in the narrative

characters.name: the giants
characters.description: Term used interchangeably with the Cyclopes in the text

characters.name: the Sirens
characters.description: Mythical singing creatures who tempt sailors (appears as a pair)

characters.name: Planctae / the Wanderers
characters.description: Perilous wandering rocks/sea‑features (Planctae), personified as the Wanderers

characters.name: Scylla
characters.description: Sea‑monster encountered by sailors in the narrative

characters.name: Charybdis
characters.description: Sea‑monster/whirlpool encountered opposite Scylla

characters.name: Circe
characters.description: Enchantress who interacts with Ulysses and his men

characters.name: Aeolus
characters.description: Ruler associated with winds (Aeolus, here distinct from Aeolus king of the winds mention)

characters.name: Teiresias
characters.description: Seer in the underworld whose prophecy is referenced

characters.name: Eumaeus
characters.description: Swineherd and loyal servant of Ulysses

characters.name: Eurymedusa
characters.description: Named individual mentioned in a story allusion (brought from Apeira)

characters.name: Melampus
characters.description: Named figure (seer) referenced in the narrative commentary

characters.name: Euryclea
characters.description: Old nurse of Ulysses' household (identified with 'the nurse' in the text)

characters.name: Eurynome
characters.description: Alternate name appearing for the household nurse in the text

characters.name: Melanthius
characters.description: Servant/goatherd who appears in the household episodes

characters.name: Melantho
characters.description: Maid of the household implicated in the narrative's punishments

characters.name: Dolius
characters.description: Named servant who is father of some household attendants

characters.name: Phemius
characters.description: Household bard whose fate is recounted

characters.name: Medon
characters.description: Herald of the house mentioned in the narrative

characters.name: Hermione
characters.description: Named daughter referenced in comparative or genealogical remarks

characters.name: Megapenthes
characters.description: Named figure referenced in family/marriage context

characters.name: Helen of Troy
characters.description: Helen (of Troy), whose presence is sought within parts of the narrative

characters.name: the Suitors
characters.description: Collective group of named antagonists courting Penelope and occupying the house

characters.name: the maids
characters.description: Collective group of household maids, including those punished/hanged

characters.name: sun-god
characters.description: The unnamed sun‑god whose cattle are referenced in the narrative (cattle of the sun‑god)
